facts.claim: For 2027, New Year's Day (元旦) falls on Friday 1 January; the statutory holiday runs 1-3 January, 3 days, with no make-up workday.

For 2027, the Spring Festival holiday runs 5 February (the eve of the lunar new year, Friday) to 13 February (the eighth day of the first lunar month, Saturday) — 9 days, with 31 January (Sunday) and 14 February (Sunday) as make-up workdays.
For 2027, Qingming (清明节) runs 3-5 April (Saturday to Monday), 3 days, with no make-up workday.
For 2027, Labour Day runs 1-5 May (Saturday to Wednesday), 5 days, with 8 May (Saturday) as a make-up workday.
For 2027, the Dragon Boat Festival (端午节) is a single day off on 9 June (Wednesday) — not stitched to a weekend.
For 2027, the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) is a single day off on 15 September (Wednesday).
For 2027, the National Day holiday runs 1-7 October (Friday to Thursday), 7 days, with 26 September (Sunday) and 9 October (Saturday) as make-up workdays.
For 2026, New Year's Day (元旦) ran 1-3 January, 3 days, with 4 January (Sunday) as a make-up workday.

For 2026, the Spring Festival holiday ran 15 February (the 28th day of the 12th lunar month Sunday) to 23 February (the 7th day of the first lunar month, Monday) — 9 days, with 14 February and 28 February as make-up workdays.
For 2026, Qingming (清明节) ran 4-6 April (Saturday to Monday), 3 days, with no make-up workday.
For 2026, Labour Day ran 1-5 May (Friday to Tuesday), 5 days, with 9 May (Saturday) as a make-up workday.
For 2026, the Dragon Boat Festival (端午节) ran 19-21 June (Friday to Sunday), 3 days.
For 2026, the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) ran 25-27 September (Friday to Sunday), 3 days.
For 2026, the National Day holiday ran 1-7 October (Thursday to Wednesday), 7 days, with 20 September (Sunday) and 10 October (Saturday) as make-up workdays.

Since 1 January 2025, all citizens get 13 days of statutory public holiday a year: 1 day for New Year's Day, 4 days for Spring Festival, 1 day for Qingming, 2 days for Labour Day, 1 day for the Dragon Boat Festival, 1 day for Mid-Autumn and 3 days for National Day.

Spring Festival is a statutory holiday of 4 days — Lunar New Year's Eve plus the first to the third day of the first lunar month — set by the 2024 amendment to the national holiday measures, in force from 1 January 2025.
Labour Day is a statutory holiday of 2 days — 1 and 2 May — set by the same 2024 amendment, in force from 1 January 2025.
National Day is a statutory holiday of 3 days — 1 to 3 October — under the national holiday measures currently in force.
Except in special cases, the working stretch immediately before or after a public holiday is generally no more than 6 consecutive days — a rule added by the 2024 amendment.
The State Council published the List of Commonly Used Standard Chinese Characters (《通用规范汉字表》) by Notice No. 23 of 2013, dated 5 June 2013 and released 19 August 2013.

The 2013 table contains 8,105 characters in three tiers: 3,500 at the first tier (basic education), 3,000 at the second, and 1,605 at the third; the notice states that character use in general Chinese social life shall follow this table.
Chinese calligraphy was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009 (ref. RL 00216).

China's official intangible-cultural-heritage documentation records calligraphy in the national nine-year compulsory curriculum, citing the Ministry of Education's Opinions on Calligraphy Education in Primary and Secondary Schools and the Guidelines for Calligraphy Education in Schools as the policy basis for survival.

China's traditional tea-processing techniques and associated social practices were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List on 29 November 2022, at the 17th session of the Intergovernmental Committee held in Rabat, Morocco.

Chinese tea is divided into 6 categories - green, yellow, dark (hei), white, oolong and black (hong) - by processing and oxidation, with a further 2,000+ products once flower-scented and reprocessed teas are counted, the wording the Ministry of Culture and Tourism uses.
The tea-processing listing is the 44th item, by 44 related national-level intangible-heritage projects, and China had 43 UNESCO intangible-heritage listings before it, ranking first in the world.

The 24 solar terms (二十四节气) were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List on 30 November 2016, at the 11th session in Addis Ababa; the element is framed as the time-knowledge system Chinese people built by observing the sun's annual motion.

The 24 solar terms were first added to the national intangible-heritage list in 2006, with sub-elements added in 2011 (Jiuhua Lichun rites, Banchun quannong, Shiqian shuo chun) and in 2014 (Sanmen jidong, Zhuang Shuangxiang festival, Miao Ganqiu, Anren ganfenshe).

Spring Festival - the social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of the traditional new year - was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List on 4 December 2024, at the 19th session in Asuncion, Paraguay.
With the Spring Festival listing, China had 44 items on UNESCO's intangible-heritage lists and registers, and the count stayed the highest in the world, as stated in the inscription report.

China's Spring Festival inscription is the 44th item on UNESCO's intangible-heritage lists - the Dragon Boat Festival (2009) and the 24 solar terms (2016) came before it, as the national intangible-heritage inventory records.

Partial public holidays: Women's Day (8 March) gives women half a day off; Youth Day (4 May) gives youth aged 14 and over half a day; Children's Day (1 June) gives children under 14 one day; Army Day (1 August) gives active service personnel half a day.
Holidays for ethnic-minority customary festivals are set by the local people's government of the relevant minority-inhabited area according to each group's customs.

Other commemorative and observance days - the February 7 Commemoration, the May 30 Movement, July 7 (the War of Resistance against Japan), September 3 (victory in the War of Resistance), September 18 (Mukden Incident), Teachers' Day, Nurses' Day, Journalists' Day and Arbor Day - are not public holidays.

That instrument was revised in November 2024, and the notice published for 2025 on 12 November 2024 records the effect: from 1 January 2025 the statutory holidays for all citizens increased by two days, one added to Spring Festival and one to Labour Day.
As of December 2024, China had 44 elements inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage lists — the most of any country.
facts.source_name: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, 文旅部)

facts.claim: China's Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in December 2024.
facts.source_name: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, 文旅部)

facts.claim: The 24 Solar Terms were inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2016.
facts.source_name: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, 文旅部)

facts.claim: Tai Chi (Taijiquan) was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2020.
facts.source_name: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, 文旅部)

facts.claim: Traditional tea processing techniques and associated social practices in China were inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2022.
facts.source_name: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, 文旅部)

facts.claim: China has 60 UNESCO World Heritage sites as of July 2025: 41 cultural, 15 natural and 4 mixed cultural-and-natural. The 60th was the Xixia Imperial Tombs, inscribed on 11 July 2025 at the 47th session of the World Heritage Committee in Paris.
facts.source_name: National Cultural Heritage Administration (国家文物局) — Xixia Imperial Tombs inscription announcement

facts.claim: The Great Wall was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1987.
facts.source_name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

facts.claim: The Forbidden City (Imperial Palace) in Beijing was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1987.
facts.source_name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

facts.claim: The Great Wall's total length is 21,196.18 km, according to the 2012 official survey by the State Administration of Cultural Heritage.
facts.source_name: State Administration of Cultural Heritage (国家文物局)

facts.claim: The Forbidden City covers about 720,000 m² (72 hectares) in central Beijing.
facts.source_name: China.org.cn (中国网)

facts.claim: At the end of 2024 China had 16,541 A-level scenic areas, including 339 rated 5A (the top grade, 19 newly rated that year); together they received 6.76 billion visits and earned CNY 481.42 billion in ticket and on-site revenue.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (文化和旅游部)

facts.claim: By the end of 2024 China had 7,046 registered museums, 91.46% of them free to enter, which welcomed 1.49 billion visits and hosted over 40,000 exhibitions that year.
facts.source_name: National Cultural Heritage Administration (国家文物局)

facts.claim: China has five national parks, all formally established on 12 October 2021: Sanjiangyuan, Giant Panda, Northeast China Tiger and Leopard, Hainan Tropical Rainforest, and Wuyishan. Together they cover about 230,000 km2 and protect nearly 30% of the country's key terrestrial wildlife and plant species.
facts.source_name: National Forestry and Grassland Administration

facts.claim: Under the National Park Spatial Layout Plan, China has 49 candidate national park areas with a total area of about 1.1 million km2, roughly 10.3% of its land territory, plus 110,000 km2 of sea.
facts.source_name: National Forestry and Grassland Administration

facts.claim: China's 2026 public holiday schedule: New Year 1-3 Jan (3 days), Spring Festival 15-23 Feb (9 days), Qingming 4-6 Apr (3 days), Labour Day 1-5 May (5 days), Dragon Boat 19-21 Jun (3 days), Mid-Autumn 25-27 Sep (3 days), National Day 1-7 Oct (7 days). Weekend swaps create these longer blocks, so travel demand peaks at the start and end of each one.
facts.source_name: General Office of the State Council

facts.claim: China has 51 UNESCO Global Geoparks — 21% of the 241 geoparks in the global network, which spans 51 countries — the largest number of any country.
facts.source_name: National Forestry and Grassland Administration (Xinhua report)

facts.claim: China has 1,557 national-level intangible cultural heritage items in five batches, within a four-tier (national, provincial, municipal, county) list of more than 100,000 items.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Culture and Tourism

facts.claim: China has recognised 3,997 national-level inheritors of intangible cultural heritage across six batches, plus 23 national cultural-ecology protection zones.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Culture and Tourism

facts.claim: China has 188 China-Nationally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (China-NIAHS) in seven batches, and 22 Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) out of 86 worldwide — the most of any country.
facts.source_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

facts.claim: The 2026 Spring Festival travel rush runs 2 February to 13 March 2026 — 40 days. National rail expects 539 million passenger trips, up 5.0% year on year, with peak days around 13 February (outbound) and 23 February (return). At peak, more than 14,000 passenger trains run per day, with 5.3% more seat capacity than the previous year.
facts.source_name: China State Railway Group – 2026 Spring Festival ticket sales announcement

facts.claim: The Xixia Imperial Tombs (西夏陵) were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 11 July 2025, at the 47th session of the World Heritage Committee held in Paris. They became China's 60th World Heritage site and were listed under criteria (ii) and (iii) as evidence of cultural exchange and of a multi-ethnic, unified state.
facts.source_name: National Cultural Heritage Administration (国家文物局) — Xixia Imperial Tombs inscription announcement

facts.claim: Xixia Imperial Tombs (西夏陵) covers nearly 40 square kilometres on the eastern slopes of the Helan Mountains south of Yinchuan, Ningxia. It contains 9 imperial tombs, 271 satellite tombs, a 5.03-hectare northern architectural site and 32 flood-control structures — the largest and best-preserved surviving archaeological remains of the Tangut Western Xia dynasty (1038-1227).
facts.source_name: National Cultural Heritage Administration (国家文物局) — report on the Xixia inscription
